title: Azure resource and evidence dependencies
alt: Structural Azure topology and evidence map. AKS has a public API endpoint with Kubernetes RBAC, managed Entra, Azure RBAC, and local accounts disabled. The dedicated VNet has separate AKS-node, delegated PostgreSQL, and private-endpoint subnets; the core Key Vault, optional BYOK Key Vault, Blob, and AMPLS endpoints use the private-endpoint subnet. The optional BYOK vault uses RBAC, purge protection, and disabled public access; only the Identity Broker workload identity receives Key Vault Secrets Officer on that vault. The core vault keeps its existing Broker and Probe Secrets User and App Routing Certificates User assignments. Blob has private platform-artifacts and session-material containers. One managed wildcard HTTPS Gateway listener serves exact-host Broker, auth, api, and Portal routes; the canonical agentweaver issuer remains unchanged, and Portal's Copilot BFF remains same-origin. The Foundation Probe Job exercises exact-version Key Vault secret redemption, a Blob object-store round trip, and Entra-authenticated PostgreSQL effects. Workspace and App Insights are in eastus2; AMPLS is global. Bicep grants the probe identity Key Vault Secrets User at the core vault, Storage Blob Data Contributor at the storage account, Log Analytics Reader at the workspace, and Monitoring Metrics Publisher at App Insights; the Events & Sessions identity receives Storage Blob Data Contributor only on session-material. The separate database migration Jobs use their migration identity; the Events & Sessions Job mirrors its runtime Sessions and Messaging settings because the host validates them before migration. Identity runtime-table permissions are separate source definitions, not live bootstrap evidence. Source image builds add a verified Linux-x64 ACS library and pinned OPA binary to Orchestrator, AgentHost, and Projects & Config, then probe each image before publication. This does not claim a live deployment or complete foundation acceptance.
